syllabus_topics: Introduction to the quantum model of the atom
Chemical bonding in diatomic molecules 	Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT)
Chemical bonding in polyatomic molecules 	Valence Bond Theory (VBT)
Intermolecular forces and properties of covalent compounds
Polymers: Structure and morphology. Polymerization reactions
Metals: Structures. Metallic bonding according to MOT: Band theory and Cohesion Energy. Metal alloys
Covalent Crystals - Bonding according to MOT: Band theory
Introduction to electrical properties: Conductors, Semiconductors and Insulators
Fundamentals of Chemical Kinetics and Thermodynamics
Corrosion and methods of protection against corrosion
Applications to the engineering course in question
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 0.3 T + 0.2 L + 0.5 E, where T is the average of 3 theoretical tests, L is the average of 2 laboratory tests, and E is the exam grade. Students are approved if NF is equal to or greater than 9.5 values, with a minimum of 7 values on the exam. For the resit exam, the final grade will be the best of NF = 0.2 L + 0.8 ER or NF = 0.3 T + 0.2 L + 0.5 ER. For special cases like worker-students, the assessment is exclusively by exam (E or ER) with a minimum grade of 9.5 values for approval.
